narratives.Overview:
Ship a Prefer-A package that:

1. Restates acceptance toward named path cases: interactive/solo PreToolUse, swarm:launch undecided or absent route file, and honor join at the actual spawn request (including launcher-argv where applicable).
2. P1 residual: place a routing conjunct ahead of every PreToolUse spawn-class allow return — spawn-explore-ready, spawn-process-only-ready, spawn-ephemeral-ready, spawn-ready, and the launcher-argv / decideLauncherFamilyArgv branch — for gated roles/providers (inherit free-text marker refuse). Make swarm:launch fail-closed when the route file is absent and when leaf is undecided (call verifyRouting or match enforce, including missing-file to undecided to EXIT_GATE_FAILED). Record --skip-routing uses.
3. P3: require an adapter/interceptor (or host PreToolUse field check / argv inspection) that validates or constructs the spawn request against the trusted route snapshot before submit; tests must show pinned route + omitted/different model cannot reach the spawn callback on covered paths. Explicitly scope what hosts and spawn classes cannot intercept (payload model vs argv model). Separate requested-model conformance from proof of the host's actual serving model. Reject token-only / advisory-only / self-attested model: as P3 closure for builders.
4. P2: decide and document the gated-role domain inside SWARM_WORKER_ROLES (or explicit subset); preserve harness-default; do not add critic to that enum; point critic auditability at the model: lead.
5. Docs honesty: AGENTS/#1877 residual names story-ready vs interactive solo and the critic/process-only role-domain carve-out; record explore either as covered by the conjunct or as a decided carve-out with subagent_type self-declaration named; if the gated domain is an explicit subset of SWARM_WORKER_ROLES, record that subset gap vs ANY; HELP_TEXT matches ROUTING_GATED_DISPATCH_PROVIDERS; either add codex to that provider set or record that the gated-provider set is narrower than LAUNCHER_FAMILIES; optional session-start --advise is additive disclosure only.
6. Alive: acceptance item recorded checked; further liveness work is a separate residual.
7. Routing authority: keep per-task overrides distinguishable from shared policy mutation; issue/envelope prose is not authority to overwrite the operator routing file; bind receipts to the trusted resolution used to construct that request.

## Second occurrence, same detection path — plus one finding that changes the remedy options

Recording a recurrence rather than filing a duplicate. This issue already describes what happened; the new part is that **invoking the gate would not have caught it.**

### The recurrence

2026-08-27. A single Cursor session dispatched five `leaf-implementation` builders — #3784, #3807, #3730, #3796, #3831 — none of which passed a model parameter, so all five silently inherited the parent (Opus 5). `verify:routing` was not invoked before any of them.

It surfaced exactly as last time: **the operator asked which models were being used.** Two instances, 2026-08-24 and 2026-08-27, same detection path, which is a human noticing rather than a mechanism firing.

The divergence was against an explicit pin, not a default:

```json
"cursor": {
  "leaf-implementation": { "model": "composer-2.5-fast", "mode": "pinned",
                           "decidedAt": "2026-07-23T22:43:34.423Z" }
}
```

Worth noting the same session's `review-monitor` dispatch was **conformant** — `cursor.review-monitor` is `harness-default`, so inheriting was the recorded decision. Only the gated pinned role diverged.

### The new finding: the gate passes while the dispatch diverges

This issue's framing is "nothing ever invokes it." That is true, and it is not the whole problem. I invoked it today, after the five dispatches:

```
routing gate: provider 'cursor' -- all gated role(s) decided.
  leaf-implementation: model composer-2.5-fast (resolved-via cursor-route)
EXIT: 0
```

**Exit 0**, with five non-conformant dispatches already made. `verify:routing` verifies that every gated role *has a decision in config*. It has no visibility into whether any dispatch *honoured* that decision, and structurally cannot — it reads `.deft/routing.local.json`, not the dispatch stream.

So an agent can invoke the gate, pass it cleanly, and dispatch on any model at all. That is the same shape as several defects found today: a check that validates the adjacent thing rather than the thing.

**This weakens the "session-start advisory" candidate** in the body above. Wiring `--advise` into `session:start` would have reported "all gated roles decided" and surfaced nothing, because the config was complete and correct the entire time. The failure was never an undecided role.

It correspondingly **strengthens the envelope-token direction**: only an artifact carrying the routing decision alongside the dispatch makes conformance observable.

### Counter-evidence for the cheapest option

The body says accepting post-hoc auditability "deserves real consideration rather than being listed for symmetry," on the grounds that the `model:` comment lead makes routing recoverable after the fact.

That holds for **critics** and not for **builders**. A critic posts a `model:` lead per #3628, so its routing is auditable. A `leaf-implementation` builder posts no comment lead anywhere — it opens a PR and writes commits, neither of which records the model. Today's five dispatches left **no artifact naming a model**; the only reason the routing is known is that I remember it.

So post-hoc auditability does not cover the one role the gate actually gates by default. The cheapest option is cheaper than it looks because it silently excludes the gated role.

Two caveats on that: the `model:` lead is itself self-reported and unreliable on at least one host (#3824), and #3815 covers the same self-attestation gap. Post-hoc auditability rests on a channel two open issues say cannot be trusted.

### Not proposing a remedy here

This is evidence for the existing arc, not a competing design. The operator's interim decision for this session is per-task routing recorded explicitly at dispatch — routine builds on the pinned route, gate/authorization/security work routed deliberately and stated — which is a behavioural stopgap, not a mechanism.

Refs #3824, #3815, #3827.

Verification: read the issue body and only comments at or below the ceiling; ran SHA-pinned source reads and `git grep` for callers, route resolution, manifest fields, and liveness wiring. This is source-path verification, not execution of fixtures or reconstruction of the historical host sessions. The August dispatch counts and model usage remain reported incident evidence, not independently measured facts here.

Existing mechanisms: `verifyRouting` checks decided/valid routes; `verify:story-ready` calls it after successful story evaluation for recognized gated providers unless routing is skipped; `swarm:launch` resolves a route and emits `dispatch_provider`, `worker_role`, `resolved_model`, and `model_source`; swarm Phase 3 already requires passing the resolved model to the actual primitive. The unresolved boundary is downstream of those preparations.

### F1 — blocks-the-design: A routing receipt must constrain the spawn, not merely accompany it

Evidence: [routing verification](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/be9f25dcdb0f2e32b93b168ec5d4d16b295d7550/packages/core/src/swarm/routing-verify.ts#L98) takes config/provider/roles, with no actual dispatch arguments. [Launch manifest emission](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/be9f25dcdb0f2e32b93b168ec5d4d16b295d7550/packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts#L1048) already records the routing fields. [Phase 3](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/be9f25dcdb0f2e32b93b168ec5d4d16b295d7550/content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-3.md#L109) explicitly distinguishes manifest preparation from passing the actual model argument. Recurrence [5447801553](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3703#issuecomment-5447801553) reports exactly this separation failing.

Failure mode: the parent records pin A, obtains a successful check or token, then invokes a native spawn with no model argument. An envelope naming A is equally compatible with that failing execution. A new self-authored receipt would reproduce the existing manifest's limitation.

Disposition: reject token-only, session-advisory-only, or manifest-only closure of P3. For a mechanically enforced slice, name an adapter/interceptor that validates or constructs the actual request before submitting it, and test that a pinned route plus omitted/different model cannot reach that adapter's spawn callback. Reuse existing route resolution and manifest vocabulary. Clearly separate requested-model conformance from proof of the host's actual serving model; the latter requires host evidence and is not supplied by critic self-attestation. If native tool calls remain outside interception, say so and scope the guarantee accordingly. This is a blocking condition on the remedy, not a claim that such an adapter already exists.

### F2 — sharpens-framing: The invocation inventory has changed; the remaining scope is path- and provider-specific

Evidence: [story-ready lines 178–199](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/be9f25dcdb0f2e32b93b168ec5d4d16b295d7550/packages/cli/src/verify-story-ready.ts#L178) invoke `verifyRouting`; [provider set](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/be9f25dcdb0f2e32b93b168ec5d4d16b295d7550/packages/core/src/swarm/routing.ts#L64) includes cursor, grok, grok-bot, openclaw, and claude. [AGENTS.md line 135](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/be9f25dcdb0f2e32b93b168ec5d4d16b295d7550/AGENTS.md#L135) now explicitly calls the broad rule behavioral doctrine. The Stop 1 correctly acknowledges shipped #1877, although its cursor/grok shorthand understates the current set. `git grep` found the direct production calls in story-ready and the routing CLI; this is not a reproduction of the older Taskfile/hooks/workflows measurement.

Failure mode: acceptance phrased as “give a gate that nothing calls an invocation point” can pass by pointing to existing story-ready wiring, while interactive native spawns still bypass it. Conversely, wiring only `swarm:launch` misses the named solo path.

Disposition: retain P1, but express acceptance as a named dispatch-path failure case rather than zero-call rhetoric. Distinguish entry-point invocation, route selection, and request conformance. Preserve existing checks and make the uncontrolled-path limitation explicit; do not relabel historical measurements as false merely because this pin differs.

### F3 — blocks-the-design: Expanding the default role list cannot by itself satisfy “ANY”

Evidence: [DEFAULT_GATED_ROLES](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/be9f25dcdb0f2e32b93b168ec5d4d16b295d7550/packages/core/src/swarm/routing-verify.ts#L30) contains only leaf-implementation. [Routing vocabulary and harness-bound policy](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/be9f25dcdb0f2e32b93b168ec5d4d16b295d7550/packages/core/src/swarm/routing.ts#L25) define four swarm roles and explicit default semantics. The pinned [design-critique contract](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/be9f25dcdb0f2e32b93b168ec5d4d16b295d7550/content/contracts/design-critique.md) expressly forbids adding a critic seat to `SWARM_WORKER_ROLES`. `verifyRouting` also deliberately permits an undecided unknown host with disclosure.

Failure mode: widening the default list either forces unrelated roles to be configured for every single dispatch or still misses critics outside that vocabulary. Treating every null model as nonconformance rejects legitimate explicit harness-default routes. Unknown-host disclosure also contradicts a claimed universal fail-closed guarantee.

Disposition: the remedy must define its dispatch-role and provider domain before claiming P2 relief. Check the role actually dispatched, preserve explicit harness-default, and explicitly choose the treatment of process-only critics and unknown hosts. Do not silently expand the swarm vocabulary or turn intentional provider exceptions into universal enforcement claims. Role coverage is separable from honor-at-dispatch, but cannot be omitted while claiming the existing ANY obligation is satisfied.

### F4 — sharpens-framing: Shared routing state needs a defined decision time and authority

Evidence: [resolveRoutingPath](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/be9f25dcdb0f2e32b93b168ec5d4d16b295d7550/packages/core/src/swarm/routing.ts#L112) deliberately reads the main worktree's shared, gitignored routing file (or an environment override). Launch resolves it before constructing a manifest; the eventual native spawn is separate.

Failure mode: sibling A prepares a request under route X while sibling B changes the shared route to Y. A later config read can falsely condemn A or approve a request whose decision was never used. An issue/envelope instruction claiming a new model is also not authority to overwrite the operator's routing choice.

Disposition: bind each controlled dispatch to the trusted resolution used to construct that request, with an explicit snapshot-versus-latest policy. metadata.issueBody:
`verify:routing` is described as a **pre-dispatch gate** — "fails when a dispatched worker role has no decision in `.deft/routing.local.json`." It is fail-closed, it is implemented, it has tests, and **nothing ever invokes it.**

AGENTS.md requires the decision it guards:

> **Deliberate model routing:** Before ANY sub-agent dispatch (cohort OR single), make a deliberate per-`worker_role` routing decision via `task verify:routing` / `task swarm:routing-set` — never silently inherit the parent model.

So the rule is stated, the mechanism is built, and the two are not connected.

## Measured at `8bb1e528`

`verify:routing` appears in **no** `Taskfile.yml` target, **no** hook under `.githooks/`, and **no** workflow under `.github/workflows/`. It runs only when an agent remembers to type it.

`DEFAULT_GATED_ROLES = ["leaf-implementation"]` (`packages/core/src/swarm/routing-verify.ts:30`), widened only by an explicit `--roles a,b` (`:99`).

`.deft/routing.local.json` exists in this clone, so a decision was recorded at some point — but nothing checked it against any dispatch.

## How it failed in practice

On 2026-08-24 a single session dispatched roughly forty sub-agents: 35 critic posts across four models, plus builders and pollers. **`verify:routing` was invoked zero times.** No gate fired, no warning appeared, and the omission surfaced only because a human asked which models were being used.

The routing decisions themselves were deliberate and are recoverable from the `model:` comment lead that #3628 and #3646 landed. That is the saving grace and it is *post-hoc* — the rule asks for a pre-dispatch decision, and nothing verified one existed.

## Two distinct gaps

**1. No invocation point.** A fail-closed gate that is never called is documentation. This is the same structural class as #3661 (a mechanized consumer with no producer obligation) and #3672 (a MUST with no completion criterion), except sharper: here a *working* fail-closed implementation exists and is simply not wired to anything.

**2. The gated role set is narrower than the rule.** AGENTS.md says "ANY sub-agent dispatch." The gate defaults to `leaf-implementation` alone. Critic dispatches — 35 posts in one day, across four different models, each a deliberate routing choice — are not in the default set and would not have been caught even if the gate had run.

## Why an invocation point is hard, and worth saying up front

`task check`, hooks and CI all run at commit or merge time. **Dispatch happens mid-session, before any of them.** So the natural enforcement surfaces are the wrong shape, and that may be exactly why this was never wired.

Candidate directions, none selected:

- **Session-start advisory.** `--advise` already exists for a non-blocking disclosure. Wiring that into `session:start` would surface undecided roles before work begins, but it is advisory and does not gate the dispatch itself.
- **Gate the dispatch verbs.** `swarm:launch` is a natural chokepoint — but the interactive solo path (#3666, #3669) deliberately does not go through it, and that path is where most of today's dispatches came from.
- **Make it a preamble obligation with a recorded token**, like the #3651 substantiation markers, so a dispatch envelope carries evidence of the decision. Costly, and the #3672 arc is a caution against adding obligations without completion criteria.
- **Accept post-hoc auditability as sufficient** and downgrade the AGENTS.md rule from "before ANY dispatch" to what is actually enforceable. Cheapest, and honest, if the pre-dispatch timing is not load-bearing.

The last one deserves real consideration rather than being listed for symmetry. If the `model:` lead makes routing auditable after the fact, and the decision quality was fine all day without the gate, the rule may be over-specified rather than under-enforced.

## Also worth checking while here

`verify:subagent-alive` (#2824) is a fail-closed liveness gate for in-flight `drive-to: merge*` workers, exiting 1 with `REDISPATCH_OK`. On the same day, three workers died to a workspace disconnect and the operator learned about it from host notifications rather than from that gate. Whether it has an invocation point either is worth confirming — it may be the same defect on a different verb.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A decision is recorded on whether pre-dispatch routing verification is enforceable, or whether the AGENTS.md rule should be restated to match what is
- [ ] If enforceable: `verify:routing` has an invocation point that fires before dispatch, and the gated role set matches the rule's scope
- [ ] If not: the AGENTS.md rule is reworded to describe an auditable-after-the-fact obligation, and the `model:` comment lead is named as the audit surface
- [ ] Either way, `verify:routing` is not left as a fail-closed gate nothing calls
- [ ] `verify:subagent-alive` is checked for the same defect
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` line

## Provenance

Found 2026-08-24 after a session dispatched ~40 sub-agents without invoking the gate, when the operator asked which models were in use. All measurements above taken at `8bb1e528`. Related: #1739 (built the routing verbs), #2824 (`verify:subagent-alive`), #3661 and #3672 (same structural class), #3702 (a rule whose skill never mentions it).
